physicalNotes: Radius 0.22419523 Jupiter radii from Palethorpe et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.548ag520P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag520P/abstract): 16,028.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.04845382 Jupiter masses (Palethorpe et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026MNRAS.548ag520P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag520P/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Palethorpe et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.548ag520P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PALETHORPE_ET_AL_2026): P 50.819172 d
sources.shape: Palethorpe et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.548ag520P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PALETHORPE_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 65.06; Palethorpe et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.548ag520P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PALETHORPE_ET_AL_2026): inclination 89.271 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Palethorpe et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.548ag520P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PALETHORPE_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459534.0662 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 4 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
